Bannister CA.role: First author of the Atlas study BAN2014 (metformin and survival in type 2 diabetes).
Bannister CA.sub: Cochrane Institute of Primary Care and Public Health, School of Medicine, Cardiff University, Cardiff, UK
story: In BAN2014 (2014), Christian Bannister is the first author. The paper is a retrospective, observational study of UK patient records. People with type 2 diabetes who started metformin lived longer, on average, than matched people without diabetes. Because it is observational, patient selection and other confounders cannot be ruled out.
In the Atlas record PubMed gives the first name only as initials (C A). Two related papers from the same Cardiff group list him as Christian A Bannister with several of the same co-authors.

Ottina KA.sub: Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research · Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA
story: BAR2013 (2013) is a cell study that found GATOR1, a protein complex that switches off the Rag proteins and so turns mTORC1 down when amino acids run low. GATOR1 genes are mutated in some cancers, which made those cancer cells keep mTORC1 on and more sensitive to rapamycin. Kathleen Ottina is a middle author in the author list. HSU2011 (2011) is a cell study that mapped which phosphate tags on proteins depend on mTOR and found that Grb10 is an mTORC1 target that helps turn down growth-factor signalling. Kathleen Ottina is a middle author in the author list.
PubMed lists Kathleen A Ottina in both records but gives no affiliation for her there. Two related papers from the same laboratory list her at the Whitehead Institute and MIT.

Campone M.sub: Institut de Cancérologie de l'Ouest, Nantes Saint Herblain, France
story: BAS2012 (2012) is BOLERO-2, a phase 3 randomised trial in 724 women with hormone-receptor-positive advanced breast cancer. Adding everolimus to exemestane roughly doubled progression-free survival (10.6 versus 4.1 months by central review). Mario Campone is a middle author in the author list. PIC2014 (2014) is the final overall-survival report of BOLERO-2. Median overall survival was 31.0 months with everolimus plus exemestane and 26.6 months with placebo plus exemestane, a difference that was not statistically significant. Mario Campone is a middle author in the author list.

PubMed gives no affiliation for this author in the BOLERO-2 primary report. The affiliation here comes from the final overall-survival report, which lists the same author by surname and initials and shares many co-authors with the primary report.

Lebwohl D.lab_name: Novartis Oncology (Florham Park, New Jersey, USA)
Lebwohl D.role: Co-author (middle position in the author list) of the Atlas studies MOT2008, BIS2013, BAS2012, YAO2011, FRA2013.
Lebwohl D.sub: Novartis Oncology, Florham Park, NJ, USA
story: MOT2008 (2008) is a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in metastatic kidney cancer in which everolimus extended median progression-free survival from 1.9 to 4.0 months. David Lebwohl is a middle author in the author list. BIS2013 (2013) is a phase 3 randomised trial (118 people) of everolimus for kidney tumours called angiomyolipomas in tuberous sclerosis complex or LAM. Tumours shrank by at least half in 42% of treated people and in none on placebo. David Lebwohl is a middle author in the author list. BAS2012 (2012) is BOLERO-2, a phase 3 randomised trial in 724 women with hormone-receptor-positive advanced breast cancer. Adding everolimus to exemestane roughly doubled progression-free survival (10.6 versus 4.1 months by central review). David Lebwohl is a middle author in the author list. YAO2011 (2011) is RADIANT-3, a phase 3 randomised trial (410 people) in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours. Everolimus raised median progression-free survival from 4.6 to 11.0 months. David Lebwohl is a middle author in the author list. FRA2013 (2013) is a phase 3 randomised trial (117 people) of everolimus for brain tumours called SEGA in tuberous sclerosis. Tumours shrank by at least half in 35% of treated people and in none on placebo. David Lebwohl is a middle author in the author list.

No Atlas record gives an affiliation for this author. The affiliation here comes from related Novartis-sponsored everolimus papers, where PubMed or the paper's own author list places the same named author at Novartis in Florham Park, New Jersey.

story: KOR2011 (2011) is a cell study showing that where lysosomes sit in the cell helps decide whether mTORC1 is on. BER2006 (2006) is a study in cells and fruit flies showing that rapamycin, by inducing autophagy, cleared several toxic aggregate-prone proteins and reduced the toxicity of tau. Fiona Menzies is a middle author in the author list.

PubMed gives no affiliation for her in these records. Related papers from the same Cambridge group list her as Fiona M Menzies, and a 2014 paper places her at the Cambridge Institute for Medical Research.
